lead_with.title: Montreal as ANZ's cost-smart North American base
lead_with.text: A Finance Montréal-commissioned Boyd study puts a 150-person financial operation at about **US$18.9M a year in Montreal vs US$35.3M in New York**, in the same time zone as ANZ's New York team.

lead_with.text: Quebec's **International Financial Centre** credit can reach **C$18,000 per eligible employee per year**, including for services provided under contract to a **foreign affiliate** (compliance, data, IT, fund and transaction support).

company.text: ANZ Group (ASX: ANZ) is an Australian bank serving retail, commercial and institutional clients in Australia, New Zealand and around 30 markets, with Institutional banking as a core strength. CEO **Nuno Matos** names Institutional as one of its two market-leading positions and its **Asia presence** as a source of diversification. Singapore is the hub for South East Asia, India and the Middle East (Country Head **Chris Raciti** since mid-2025). In the US, ANZ's New York team (Country Head **John McLean**, appointed Dec 2025) supports trade and investment flows with Australia, New Zealand and Asia, and covers local and international banks.

financials.text: FY2025 (year ended **Sep 30, 2025**): statutory profit **A$5.89bn** (down 10%), cash profit **A$5.79bn**, or **A$6.90bn** excluding significant items (flat; significant items of A$1.1bn included an ASIC settlement and restructuring). Full-year dividend **166 cents** per share; **CET1 12.0%**. FY2026 results are due in early **November 2026** (date to be confirmed): check them before the meeting. Context: a large, well-capitalised group under **cost and restructuring pressure**, which supports a cost-saving location pitch.

talking_points: How does ANZ serve **Canadian clients and banks** today: from New York, or not at all?
Is ANZ reviewing where it locates **operations, compliance, data or tech roles** that support the US business or the group?
